records.deidentified_narrative: on march 7, 2023 at approximately 2000 hours, police responded to a report of a major accident at 1053 penberthy bl. (30. 600853, -96. 345899). the reporting party advised that a vehicle had struck a pedestrian in a crosswalk at the penberthy intermural fields. witnesses stated that they were friends with unit 2 and were walking east bound across penberthy bl. towards pa 100m. i asked what they had observed about the vehicle, a gold buick lesabre. i was told that the vehicle appeared to be traveling faster than 20 mph and had hit unit 2 in the right leg area. the witness further stated that he observed unit 2 flip after being stuck and that he had landed on either his shoulders or head. unit 1 advised that he believed that he was speeding and was driving at approximately 30 mph at the time of the accident. when i asked if he had seen unit 2 in the crosswalk, unit 1 stated that he had been looking down to change a song on his phone. i asked if unit 1 had consumed any alcohol, the driver stated no. i asked unit 1 had taken any prescription medications or other drugs, unit 1 stated no. the hood of the vehicle was covered in a thin layer of dust, except for a section that had made contact with unit 2. there was no dents or scraps on the hood, just the dust being wiped off. i observed and photographed damage to the windshield at the drivers side a-pillar. the windshield had been fractured from the outside of the vehicle and had a spider web type pattern. the damaged covered the entire lower corner of the windshield with the center of the damage being close to the corner of the windshield. this was a result of unit 2 striking the windshield after being struck. it is not clear at this time which part of unit 2 shattered the windshield.

about to walk across the main private roadway that goes directly in front of listed locations entrance when he observed unit1 coming from his right. the pedestrian stated he waved unit1 on and began to walk towards the rear of unit1 to allow them to pass in front of him. per listed pedestrian own words he stated unit1 intentionally hit the gas and turned right in front of him. the pedestrian stated he put his hands out in front of him atop unit1's hood and unit1 came to a complete stop. listed pedestrian stated unit1's driver stated they were sorry as they drove off. listed pedestrian wanted to report the incident because he is now having left wrist and lower back pain. the accounts of the incident that the pedestrian gave sounded as if unit1 intentionally tried to hit him. listed location does have video surveillance. i contacted listed location loss prevention manager who is listed on my call for [case id]. loss prevention showed me the recorded video surveillance of the incident. after reviewing the video surveillance i observed listed pedestrian walking across the parking lot as he was waving unit1 to pass by as he was walking. the pedestrian began to walk towards the rear of unit1 as if he [roadway] forward but unit1 began to turn down the parking isle that the pedestrian redirected towards. that's when both unit1 and listed pedestrian were face to face with each other. the pedestrian placed his hands on unit1's hood and unit1 came to an immediate stop. the pedestrian without hesitation removed his hands from the hood and began to walk pass unit1 as the front right passenger window of unit1 began to roll down in an apparent attempt of the driver to contact the pedestrian. the pedestrian continued walking and did not attempt to grab a license plate or driver information. unit1 drove away from the location. the pedestrian refused ems. i contacted tid det. p. thomas #2093 and advised him of the incident and video surveillance. i was advised that there was no offense for failure to stop/render aid. i was to only generate a crash report. i gave the pedestrian the [case id], no further action taken. coban/bwc activated.

[person] reported to have initially complied and while the officers were attending to officer joseph, she left location without providing information. officer joseph was medically evaluated by sale first aid [medical facility], despite being treated for ""road rash"" on his left arm. officer lorenzo herrera who was assigned at the e gate officer's station, west of the entrance, advised me he witnessed a ""florence texas"" [school facility] district vehicle leaving the location after the officer was struck. i located the listed suspect vehicle at the livestock barns and made contact with [person], who was advised she left the scene of a crash failing to render aid in violation of texas penal code. [person] denied leaving the scene and advised she did stop to check officer joseph's welfare and indicated officer joseph immediately stood up and returned to work. she also claimed she believed she was told to leave the location, and informed me [person] present when the crash occurred and witnessed her stop to render aid to officer joseph. i asked [person] sit in my vehicle while i made contact with [person]. i made contact with [person], who was driving directly behind [person]. [person] he witnessed [person] sharply at the entrance in an effort to avoid an exiting vehicle and strike officer joseph on the shoulder. he continued to say he observed officer joseph fall under the trailer and advised he, [person] a third person all exited their vehicles to see if he was injured. he advised officer joseph advised he was fine and picked up his wand returning to work. he also indicated they were advised to clear the location by an officer on scene, and informed me he believed that to mean they could leave because officer joseph was not injured. i made contact with officer's huff and martinez who informed me [person] exit her vehicle and ask if officer joseph was okay. officer martinez informed me she instructed [person] pull off to the side and wait for them, but instead [person] the location. i observed officer martinez to be wearing a bwc and asked if she recorded the incident. officer martinez informed me she did not have any bwc footage of the incident. [person] allowed to continue to load her items and [case id] was provided to officer johnson. officer [medical facility] by san antonio ems at 0000 hours.

records.deidentified_narrative: during my regular patrol routine, police responded to the above listed location for a major crash involving a pedestrian. upon making the listed location, i made contact with pedestrian (pedestrian's personal information was listed on my kc). the listed pedestrian was laying on the ground behind unit 1. i spoke to the pedestrian who stated her daughter was driving unit 1. pedestrian stated unit 1 was backing out of the parking spot to give the back door more room to open. as unit 1 was backing out of the parking spot, pedestrian's grandson went behind unit 1 as it was reversing. the listed pedestrian was able to grab the child as it was getting behind unit 1 as it was backing up. pedestrian stated she fell and unit 1 ran over her leg with the back tire. pedestrian stated the vehicle got on top of her left leg and then went forward. as i was talking to the pedestrian, i observed apparent bruising to appear on her leg. unit 1 driver stated she was backing up and did not realize that pedestrian nor her son was behind unit 1 as she was backing up. unit 1 driver stated pedestrian was able to shove [roadway] so her son did not get hit but pedestrian fell upon unit 1 reversing out of the parking spot. med medic #1 made it to the location and provided medical attention to pedestrian. i was able to call det. martinez #2477 who is assigned to traffic investigations and advised her of the incident. unit 1 driver was given a [case id] for her records [medical facility] for better treatment. no further actions taken.
